To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

burnout is characterized by emotional exhaustion, depersonalization, and diminished sense of personal accomplishment; that these three aspects of burnout are empirically distinguishable; and that burnout is associated with both work and nonwork stressors.

(1 ) burnout has three major dimensions (emotional exhaustion, depersonalization, and reduced personal accomplishment) (2) burnout is associated with both work and family stressors and (3) burnout is also linked to personal and organizational outcomes, such as health, turnover, and job satisfaction.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and testing of a model of burnout, and the application of this model to organizational settings.
understanding the causes, correlates, and consequences of burnout.
burnout in organizational settings, particularly among people who are in service-providing jobs
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we do not know enough to give definitive answers about the nature and causes of burnout, nor do we have the knowledge needed to develop effective interventions.
burnout is a serious occupational hazard that can have serious negative effects on both the worker and the organization.
we have made progress in our understanding of burnout and in the development of measures to assess it, and that we have begun to identify some of the correlates of burnout.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
burnout is a complex phenomenon, with different aspects having different antecedents, correlates, and consequences.

(1 ) burnout is not simply a single, monolithic phenomenon, (2) burnout is not a pathological state but rather a response to chronic work conditions, and (3) burnout is associated with a number of negative consequences.
burnout is a multidimensional syndrome, consisting of three components: emotional exhaustion, depersonalization, and reduced personal accomplishment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
burnout is not a simple phenomenon, nor is it a single entity that can be measured with a simple index. Rather
there is no single cause of burnout, and no simple solution to it.
burnout is a syndrome that consists of a number of interrelated aspects.
